description: Get what is popular on Steam right now as a ranked list. `chart` picks one: top_sellers (weekly best-sellers, with weeks on chart), most_played (top 100 by peak players on the last full day, with the rank a week earlier), most_played_deck (top 100 played on Steam Deck in the past week, with the previous week's rank) or concurrent_players (top 100 by players in game right now, live). Use for 'what's hot / top selling / most played on Steam (Deck)'; for one known game's live count use get_current_players, for the store front page's curated sections (also hardware and bundles) use get_featured, to FILTER the catalog by discount, tags or compat use discover_games. Returns only rank, appid, name, store_url and chart metrics (no price/reviews/Deck status) — pass the appids to get_items for those. `last_week_rank` null means a new entry; concurrent_players has none. Results are cached for a few minutes. top_sellers is global by default; give `country` for that country's own best-sellers and `week` for a past week. The other three are global rankings of the current period only. No API key required.

chart.description: top_sellers = weekly best-sellers; most_played = yesterday's peak players; most_played_deck = most played on Steam Deck this past week; concurrent_players = live players now.

country.description: top_sellers only: two-letter country code for that country's best-sellers, e.g. DE. Omit for the global chart. Must be a real Steam store region — the two-letter shape is all that's checked here, and Steam answers an unrecognized code with US prices rather than an error, so a typo returns plausible numbers for the wrong country.

limit.description: How many top entries to return (1-100). Default 20.

week.description: top_sellers only: any date (YYYY-MM-DD) inside the week to show; Steam's weeks start Tuesday 00:00 UTC and go back 10+ years. Omit for the latest published week (`as_of` says which week that is).

name: get_charts

as_of.description: ISO 8601 UTC time of the chart: start of the week (top_sellers), start of the day the peak was measured (most_played) or last live update (concurrent_players); null for most_played_deck, which Steam sends undated.

consecutive_weeks.description: Consecutive weeks on the weekly top-sellers chart, counting this one.

last_week_rank.description: Rank one week earlier; null means the game was not on this chart then (new entry).

name.description: Game name; null when Steam sends none for the entry.
